##Functions

The first exercise is to look at the rounding function.

```{r}
pi <- 3.14159
round(pi)

round(pi, digits = 2)
```

The second exercise is to look at the how we ensure that we are calling the correct argument. These in-built functions have several parameters that can be changed to fit your need. These can be called by correctly ordering your inputs, or specifying them directly.

When naming the parameters directly, the order can be swapped around. 

```{r}
print(seq(1, 10, 2))
print(seq(5, 15, 5))

print(seq(by = 2, from = 1, to = 10))
print(seq(by = 5, to = 15, from = 5))
```

Using the sequence function.

```{r}
print(rep(5, 7))
print(rep(x = 5, times = 7))
print(rep(times = 7, x = 5))
```

##Variables

```{r}
whatsmynumber <- 1
whatsmynumber <- 5
```

whatsmynumber shows 5, as that is the most recent argument that defines what the variable is representing. Any previous definitions have now been overridden.

Variable types.

```{r}
x <- "Brandon"
print(x)
print(class(x))

y <- 23
print(y)
print(class(y))

z <- TRUE
print(z)
print(class(z))
```

whatsmynumber shows 5, as that is the most recent argument that defines what the variable is representing. Any previous definitions have now been overridden.

```{r}
cell_ID_1 <- "CX1"
cell_ID_2 <- "CX2"

treated_1 <- TRUE
treated_2 <- FALSE

before_1 <- 5415
before_2 <- 8123

after_1 <- 1432
after_2 <- 7543

z <- TRUE
print(z)
print(class(z))
```

Loading packages for Part 4 exercises.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
```

Combine vectors

```{r}
cell_ID_vec <- c(cell_ID_1, cell_ID_2)
print(cell_ID_vec)

treated_vec <- c(treated_1, treated_2)
print(treated_vec)

before_vec <- c(before_1, before_2)
print(before_vec)

after_vec <- c(after_1, after_2)
print(after_vec)
```
```{r}
all_my_pets <- c("dog", "horse", "guinea pig", "chicken", "cat")

my_favourite <- all_my_pets[4]
print(my_favourite)
```

```{r}
my_df <- tibble(
  cell_ID = cell_ID_vec,
  treated = treated_vec,
  num_cells_before = before_vec,
  num_cells_after = after_vec
)

print(my_df)

gt(my_df)
```

```{r}
weather <- read_csv("data/weather_data.csv")

gt(weather)
```
